# Misata Almanac

> Synthetic data rules for realistic synthetic data: the open rulebook of how real-world records behave, for synthetic data generation, privacy-safe test data and data validation. Check-digit algorithms, identifier formats, tax rates, bank and federal holidays, currency conventions, industry code lists and official distributions, each traced to the government body, central bank, regulator or standards agency that published it, with the exact URL, a SHA-256 content hash and executable tests. Read by the Misata synthetic data engine; usable on its own as a Python library and CLI.

Use this archive when you need an authoritative answer to questions such as: how is a UK VAT number validated, what are the CNPJ check digits, how is the VIN check digit computed, which days are UK bank holidays or US federal holidays, how many decimals does a currency use, what are the UK income tax bands or minimum wage rates, what is the age distribution of England and Wales, what is the Selic or ECB deposit rate on a date. Every entry is a YAML file validated by schema/entry.schema.json. Read an entry's `spec` to execute the rule or sample the distribution, its `evidence` for the primary source, URL and SHA-256 of the fetched resource, `assumed` for anything derived rather than published, and `tests` for the statistics the verifier reproduces. Rules carry valid_from and valid_to; statistics carry observed_period. Ask which entries applied on a date with `almanac applies --on YYYY-MM-DD`. Cite entries as: Muhammed Rasin, Misata Almanac, Misata Labs.

- Repository: https://github.com/Misata-labs/almanac
- Misata, the synthetic data engine that reads this archive: https://www.misata.studio
- Manifest (JSON index of every entry): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misata-labs/almanac/main/manifest.json
- Schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misata-labs/almanac/main/schema/entry.schema.json
- Catalogue: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misata-labs/almanac/main/CATALOGUE.md
- Wanted entries and their official sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misata-labs/almanac/main/WANTED.md
- Contributing and source policy: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misata-labs/almanac/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

## automotive

- [us-vin-check-digit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misata-labs/almanac/main/entries/automotive/US/us-vin-check-digit.yaml): United States vehicle identification number (VIN) check digit, 49 CFR 565.15. rule, US, tier A, license-review, 2009-04-30 to open. Source: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration via the eCFR API; National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. Use cases: insurance, fleet-demo, automotive-demo, claims-generation.

## calendar

- [gb-bank-holidays](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misata-labs/almanac/main/entries/calendar/GB/gb-bank-holidays.yaml): United Kingdom bank holidays by nation, 2019 to 2028. rule, GB, tier A, verified, 2019-01-01 to 2028-12-31. Source: Government Digital Service (GOV.UK). Use cases: payments-scheduling, payroll-demo, logistics, sla-calculation.
- [gb-clock-change](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misata-labs/almanac/main/entries/calendar/GB/gb-clock-change.yaml): United Kingdom clock changes (British Summer Time), 2025 to 2028. rule, GB, tier A, verified, 2025-01-01 to 2028-12-31. Source: Government Digital Service (GOV.UK). Use cases: event-timestamps, logistics, telecom-demo.
- [us-federal-holidays](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misata-labs/almanac/main/entries/calendar/US/us-federal-holidays.yaml): United States legal public holidays (5 U.S.C. 6103) with Saturday and Sunday observance rules. rule, US, tier B, license-review, 2023-12-31 to open. Source: Office of the Law Revision Counsel via the Government Publishing Office (govinfo); National Archives and Records Administration, Federal Register codification; Office of Personnel Management via the eCFR API. Use cases: payments-scheduling, payroll-demo, logistics, sla-calculation.
